analysis.title: Positioning Intelligence | Weekly Wrap: Extreme HF selling...watching for broader capitulation (November 20th, 2026)
key_insights: JPM Prime Finance estimates hedge funds fell another 1.5% on Nov 20 and could be down more than 3% over 5 days, the worst 5-day return since Apr 7, 2025. MTD returns are estimated at -4%.
The losses are driven by beta rather than alpha, unlike Oct and early Nov. JPM says this makes the week similar to early Apr 2025 and early Aug 2024.
5d and 63d HF returns are below -3z. HF alpha is more neutral, partly because HFs de-risked earlier.
Gross flows have rebounded from prior lows and are back in line with average US seasonality, with additions across most regions this past week.

Last week's question of whether the Semis sell-off is over is answered 'no'. JPM sees the 2018 analog increasingly in focus, given 4Q selling and a reversal to roughly flat YTD. The S&P bounced briefly in late Nov 2018 before selling off more in Dec.

Global HF net selling is around -2z over 20 days and exceeds 2z in North America. Historically, large HF net selling coinciding with a market sell-off has been followed by a rebound within a month, but that has not happened yet.

The decline in net leverage from 12-month highs is comparable to the most extreme episodes since 2018, with the 8-week change around -2z. Net leverage is at the 26th percentile over five years for All Strategies.

Broader capitulation is not confirmed by US TPM, at least before Friday. The 4-week change was about -1z as of Thursday, above the -1.5z trigger. The level is at the 13th percentile since 2015, near YTD lows and closer to April 2025 levels but above more severe washout levels.
CTA risk has been reduced but not extremely. Asset managers appear to be maintaining futures exposure.
Global positioning is below the 20th percentile in every region, with the global level near the 10th percentile and -1.5z, in line with lows since 2022. The drawdown remains relatively shallow.
Japan continued to be sold and moved lower. China/Hong Kong remains near its lows and Europe is also relatively low.

Semis remain the most net-sold US group over the past 2 months, though US selling slowed to less than -1z this week. US Semis positioning is back near its long-term average, the 63rd percentile since 2018 and 0z, and at its lowest since May 2025.

US net buying this week favored Utilities, Telecom, Pharma & Biotech, FBT and Real Estate, a defensive rotation. Positioning in Consumer Staples Distribution & Retail is at historical highs and Healthcare has also benefited recently.
JPM says broader capitulation may have happened on Nov 20 and it will watch how positioning evolves.

tension_points.bull_case: HF net risk reduction is at a magnitude historically associated with a bounce. Large HF net selling during a sell-off has typically been followed by a rebound over the next month. Perhaps capitulation happened on Nov 20.
tension_points.bear_case: The expected rebound has not happened yet, and the Semis sell-off is not over. The 2018 analog suggests a brief bounce followed by more selling in December. US TPM's 4-week change (about -1z) has not reached the -1.5z trigger and positioning is above severe washout levels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: US TPM 4-week change breaching the -1.5z trigger would confirm broader capitulation. The report does not name a level that invalidates the bounce case.
